basic_details.scholarship_name: KAIST International Graduate Scholarship & Full Tuition Assistantship
basic_details.offering_entity: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology (KAIST) & Ministry of Science and ICT (MSIT), South Korea
basic_details.host_institutions_covered: KAIST Main Campus (Daejeon) and Seoul Campus (South Korea)
basic_details.major_restrictions: College of Natural Sciences (Physics, Chemistry, Mathematical Sciences), College of Life Science and Bioengineering, College of Engineering (Mechanical, Aerospace, Electrical, Computer Science, Chemical and Biomolecular, Materials Science, Civil and Environmental), and College of AI.
basic_details.number_of_awards_total: ~300 to 450 international graduate scholarships awarded annually across departments
basic_details.number_of_awards_pakistan: Extensive international cohort; typically 35 to 60 Pakistani STEM, computing, and engineering researchers selected annually
basic_details.duration_of_scholarship: 4 semesters (2 years) for Master's; 8 semesters (4 years) for PhD; 10 semesters (5 years) for Combined MS/PhD
basic_details.monthly_stipend_amount: KRW 350,000 / month institutional base stipend plus laboratory RA stipend: Total monthly living allowance typically KRW 1,000,000 to 1,500,000 / month for Master's (~PKR 210,000 to 315,000 / month) and KRW 1,400,000 to 2,000,000 / month for PhD (~PKR 294,000 to 420,000 / month), combined with 100% full tuition fee waiver

nationality_requirements: International applicants whose parents both hold non-Korean citizenship (Pakistan fully eligible)
eligibility_requirements.age_limit_notes: No statutory maximum age limit, though priority is given to young researchers with strong academic momentum.
eligibility_requirements.academic_qualifications: Recognized 16-year Bachelor's degree with minimum CGPA 3.30/4.00 for Master's; recognized 18-year Master's degree with minimum CGPA 3.30/4.00 for PhD from an HEC-recognized university.
eligibility_requirements.grading_conversion_notes: Minimum CGPA 3.30 / 4.00; selected candidates at KAIST typically hold CGPA >= 3.65 / 4.00 or top 5-10% class rank.
eligibility_requirements.subject_background_prerequisites: Computer science, electrical engineering, artificial intelligence, mechanical engineering, aerospace, physics, chemistry, materials science, or chemical engineering.
eligibility_requirements.current_education_status: Graduated or final-year students completing degree requirements before semester start.
eligibility_requirements.work_experience_notes: Prior publications in peer-reviewed scientific journals (SCI/SCIE) or top conferences (NeurIPS, ICML, CVPR, IEEE) provide a massive competitive advantage.
eligibility_requirements.language_notes: IELTS Academic minimum 6.5, TOEFL iBT minimum 83, TOEIC 720+, or official English Medium of Instruction (MOI) certificate from an accredited university.
eligibility_requirements.other_language_requirements: Korean language proficiency is not required; 100% of graduate courses and research at KAIST are conducted in English.
eligibility_requirements.gender_specific_requirements: Open equally to all qualified applicants.
eligibility_requirements.special_eligibility_categories: Applicants select 'KAIST Scholarship' directly on the online admission portal; all admitted international students are automatically considered for full scholarship.
eligibility_requirements.previous_scholarship_restrictions: Cannot hold another parallel government fellowship covering identical costs.

tuition_fee.details: 100% full tuition fee waiver covering all standard degree semesters at KAIST.
tuition_fee.amount: 100% covered (~KRW 8,000,000 to 10,000,000 / semester value; ~PKR 3,360,000 to 4,200,000 / year)

admission_application_fee.details: Online application fee of USD 80 (or KRW 80,000) paid via credit card on the KAIST portal.

accommodation.details: On-campus international graduate dormitory housing in Daejeon (twin-occupancy rooms approx. KRW 120,000 to 180,000 / month), paid easily from living stipend.

monthly_stipend.details: Combined institutional and lab research stipend: KRW 1,000,000 to 1,500,000 / month for Master's (~PKR 210,000 to 315,000 / month); KRW 1,400,000 to 2,000,000 / month for PhD (~PKR 294,000 to 420,000 / month).

airfare.details: International travel between Pakistan and Seoul Incheon International Airport is self-funded.

visa_fee.details: South Korean D-2 Student Visa fee paid directly to the Korean Embassy in Islamabad.

health_insurance.details: Mandatory enrollment in Korea National Health Insurance Service (NHIS); subsidized monthly premium (approx. KRW 70,000 / month) paid from stipend.

food_allowance.details: Extensive subsidized on-campus cafeterias at Daejeon campus, including dedicated Muslim-friendly dining cafeteria (Kaimaru); meals cost KRW 4,000 to 6,000.

books_and_materials_allowance.details: Full access to KAIST Main Library, supercomputing facilities, state-of-the-art nanofabrication cleanrooms (KANC), and research equipment.

research_funding_conference_grant.details: Laboratory research grants and national project budgets cover international conference registration, travel, and accommodation for accepted papers.

travel_transit_allowance.details: Free campus shuttle buses connecting KAIST Main Campus, Munji Campus, and local transit centers.

university_and_program_options.single_or_multiple_universities: Single South Korea #1 premier science and technology research institution (KAIST, Daejeon).
participating_institutions: KAIST Main Campus (Yuseong-gu, Daejeon) and Seoul Campus (Hongneung), South Korea
university_and_program_options.university_rankings_scope: QS World University Rankings #53 globally, #1 in South Korea for Engineering & Technology, World Top 20 for Materials Science and Electrical Engineering.
available_majors: Master's / PhD in School of Computing
Master's / PhD in Kim Jaechul Graduate School of AI
Master's / PhD in School of Electrical Engineering
Master's / PhD in Department of Mechanical Engineering
Master's / PhD in Department of Materials Science and Engineering
Master's / PhD in Department of Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering
Master's / PhD in Department of Physics and Mathematical Sciences
university_and_program_options.program_duration: Master's: 2 years; PhD: 4 years; Combined MS/PhD: 5 years
university_and_program_options.admission_requirements_summary: Bachelor's / Master's degree with CGPA >= 3.30/4.00, academic transcripts, statement of purpose, two recommendation letters, English test score (IELTS 6.5+ / TOEFL 83+ / MOI), and CV.
university_and_program_options.easiest_hardest_institutions_guidance: School of Computing, Graduate School of AI, and Electrical Engineering are exceptionally selective; contacting professors before or during application significantly increases selection likelihood.
university_and_program_options.strategic_program_match_advice: Examine current projects of KAIST laboratory principal investigators, email professors citing recent journal papers, and express willingness to contribute to their specific funded research tasks.

application_process_roadmap.account_creation_instructions: Register on the KAIST graduate admissions portal during open intake, select 'KAIST Scholarship' funding track, complete forms, upload digital documents, pay USD 80 fee, and dispatch hard-copy certified dossier to Admissions Office.
step_by_step_workflow: Step 1: Explore KAIST departmental research laboratories and contact prospective professors with CV and research interests (July for Spring / December for Fall).
Step 2: Create account on KAIST Online Graduate Admissions System.
Step 3: Complete online application, write statement of financial resources selecting KAIST Scholarship, and pay USD 80 fee.
Step 4: Register two recommenders who submit online recommendation letters.
Step 5: Send certified hard-copy documents (degrees, transcripts, apostille/attestations) via DHL to KAIST Admissions Office in Daejeon.
Step 6: Departmental admissions committee reviews applications and conducts virtual technical interviews if required.
Step 7: Final admission and scholarship award results announced online.
Step 8: Obtain Certificate of Admission (CoA), apply for South Korean D-2 visa, and arrive in Daejeon.
application_process_roadmap.university_vs_scholarship_routing: Integrated Institutional Route: Admission and KAIST Scholarship are evaluated simultaneously as a unified decision.
application_process_roadmap.recommendation_letters_submission_method: Submitted online by two recommenders via confidential portal links.
application_process_roadmap.personal_statement_prompts: Statement of Purpose (prescribed KAIST format) detailing academic background, research interests, career vision, and why KAIST is the ideal institution.
application_process_roadmap.study_plan_research_proposal_requirement: Structured research statement outlining technical focus areas, proposed methodologies, and alignment with target KAIST research labs.
application_process_roadmap.cv_format_requirements: Standard academic CV detailing education, laboratory competencies, programming skills, honors, and publications.
application_process_roadmap.interview_format_details: Online technical interview via Zoom conducted by departmental faculty committee or prospective lab PI.
application_process_roadmap.standardized_tests: IELTS Academic 6.5+, TOEFL iBT 83+, TOEIC 720+, or English Medium of Instruction (MOI) certificate accepted.
application_process_roadmap.attestation_requirements: HEC and MoFA Pakistan attestations required, followed by Korean Embassy consular legalization in Islamabad or Apostille.
application_process_roadmap.translation_requirements: Certified English or Korean translation for all non-English/non-Korean documents.
application_process_roadmap.final_submission_method: Dual submission: Online portal application followed by mandatory postal dispatch of certified physical dossier to KAIST.

required_documents_checklist.specification: Complete Bachelor's / Master's degree certificates and transcripts with CGPA >= 3.30/4.00.
required_documents_checklist.pakistan_specific_instruction: Attested by HEC, MoFA, and consular legalized by Korean Embassy Islamabad.

Confidential evaluation letters from academic professors submitted electronically.
IELTS Academic 6.5+, TOEFL iBT 83+, or official English Medium of Instruction (MOI) certificate.
Comprehensive academic CV detailing publications, research projects, technical skills, and awards.
Family Registration Certificate (FRC) and copies of passports of applicant and parents.

important_dates_timeline.document_submission_deadline: September 27 / April 12 (Hard copy postal arrival in Daejeon)
important_dates_timeline.annual_cycle_notes: Bi-annual intake: Spring semester starts in March, Fall semester starts in September.

selection_process_and_weights.academic_weight: 35% (Prior CGPA, academic rigor in STEM/computing, university standing)
selection_process_and_weights.research_experience_weight: 40% (Technical research capability, publications, programming skills, research proposal)
selection_process_and_weights.personal_statement_weight: 5% (Clarity of vision and alignment with KAIST research frontiers)
selection_process_and_weights.selection_panel_composition: KAIST Departmental Admissions Committee, School Graduate Deans, and Admissions Board.
selection_process_and_weights.evaluation_methodology: Rigorous holistic evaluation assessing mathematical ability, research productivity, experimental aptitude, and alignment with faculty laboratories.

competitiveness_profile.total_annual_applicants: ~3,500 to 4,500 international applicants across both intakes
competitiveness_profile.total_scholarships_awarded: ~300 to 450 fully funded international awards annually
competitiveness_profile.acceptance_rate_pakistan: ~12.0% to 16.0% for applicants with strong research profiles and CGPA >= 3.60
competitiveness_profile.typical_successful_applicant_gpa: Undergraduate/Master's CGPA >= 3.60 / 4.00, accompanied by strong programming skills or publications
competitiveness_profile.typical_academic_and_research_profile: Graduates with exceptional academic records in computer science, engineering, or physics, documented project experience, and professor alignment.
competitiveness_profile.common_backgrounds_of_winners: Graduates from top Pakistani universities (NUST, FAST-NUCES, UET Lahore, GIKI, PIEAS, COMSATS, Quaid-i-Azam).
competitiveness_profile.high_representation_countries: Pakistan, Vietnam, China, India, Indonesia, Turkey, Iran, Kazakhstan, Russia.

fake_websites_and_scams: Only apply through official portal admission.kaist.ac.kr.
KAIST does not work with third-party agents; all applications must be submitted directly by the candidate.
red_flags_and_warnings.application_fee_warning: Application fee of USD 80 is paid directly through the secure KAIST online portal.
red_flags_and_warnings.agent_and_intermediary_warnings: Applications prepared by commercial agents are rejected; authentic personal statements and research experience are essential.
hidden_costs_breakdown: NADRA FRC and document attestations (HEC, MoFA, Korean Embassy): ~PKR 35,000 to 50,000.
DHL document courier to South Korea: ~PKR 12,000.
Initial living deposit before first stipend payment: ~KRW 500,000 (~PKR 105,000).
misleading_claims_debunked: Myth: Korean TOPIK certificate is needed. Reality: 100% of graduate education at KAIST is conducted in English.
Myth: Flights are included. Reality: Airfare to South Korea is self-funded by the student.
official_vs_unofficial_discrepancies: Unofficial sites claim KAIST requires GRE; GRE is optional and not mandatory for international graduate admissions.

scholarship_obligations_and_terms.minimum_gpa_maintenance: Maintain minimum semester GPA of 2.70 out of 4.30 to retain the tuition waiver each semester.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.attendance_requirements: Full-time physical research presence at KAIST campus; daily participation in laboratory research activities.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.academic_progress_monitoring: Semi-annual academic progress review evaluated by research advisor.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.work_restrictions_during_study: Off-campus employment is restricted under Korean immigration law; part-time work requires permission from immigration and university.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.home_country_return_obligation: None; graduates are eligible for Korean D-10 job seeker visas or E-7 professional engineering visas upon graduation.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.service_obligations_or_bonds: Zero service bond or repayment obligation.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.repayment_clawback_conditions: Tuition waiver is cancelled if semester GPA drops below 2.70 or if student is dismissed for disciplinary infractions.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.rules_for_changing_major: Major change requires approval from current advisor, new advisor, and department heads.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.extension_policy: Extensions beyond standard 4 semesters (Master's) or 8 semesters (PhD) are generally not covered by the scholarship.
